title: Adaptive on-call runbook templates for multi-region load-shedding and circuit-breaker escalation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a templating layer that produces context-aware on-call runbooks at incident time. Templates are populated from the SLO signal (error budget burn rate, latency percentiles), region topology (primary/secondary regions, recent failovers), and the runtime circuit breaker state. The goal is to reduce noisy paging by giving operators a compact, actionable checklist tailored to the incident severity & scope, and to enable gated automated mitigations (controlled load-shedding, per-route rate caps, and dynamic circuit-breaker tightening).

Why now:
- We still see noisy multi-region pages during transient failures where a single noisy route causes global escalate cascades.
- Existing runbooks are static and require manual pruning under pressure.
- We can safely automate a small set of mitigations if we attach strict guardrails derived from SLO telemetry.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
1) Automated template generation that includes: impacted routes, SLO burn metrics (5m/30m/6h), active circuit-breaker reasons, recommended mitigations (soft: increase retry backoff, hard: per-route shed 10% traffic), suggested rollout gates, and links to observability artifacts.
2) Pager noise reduction: staging test shows >=40% reduction in pages for synthetic region blips vs current baseline.
3) On-call ergonomics: time-to-first-action (operator sees templated runbook in incident UI) < 30s after alert grouping completes.
4) Safe automation: automated mitigations must be run under two modes: auto-execute (for P3/P2 low-risk flows with canary) and gated-confirm (for P1/high blast risk). Automation should be reversible and have an immediate undo path.
5) Integration tests: end-to-end test in chaos lab covering multi-region failover, circuit-breaker tripping, and load-shedding flow with observable rollback.

Scope / Out of scope:
- IN SCOPE: runbook template engine, integrations with SLO dashboard, alert grouping service, operator UI (incident view), and a small set of automation hooks (weight adjuster, route rate limiter, retry-policy patch).
- OUT OF SCOPE: full rewrite of paging throttler, new incident commander workflow, new access control systems.

Design notes:
- Template inputs: incident_id, top_3_impacted_routes, region_map, slo_snapshot (5m/30m/6h), cb_state, recent_deploys, traffic_loss_percent, top_n_logs (first 100 lines), suggested_kill_switch.
- Decision logic: use a ruleset with precedence: safety blocks (lb health > 50% failure in a region -> require manual confirm), automated soft-mitigation threshold (slo_burn_rate > 5x and region-local -> eligible for auto-shed), global cascade detection (multi-region correlation score > 0.7 -> require manual confirm).
- Automation primitives to implement: /api/v1/route/shrink-weight, /api/v1/route/set-rate-limit, /api/v1/runtime/kv-flip for circuit-breaker tuning. Each primitive must record audit events and expose a quick rollback call.
- UI: incident panel must show the instantiated template, clearly labeled automated steps, and a one-click "apply mitigation" with a confirmation modal that lists potential customer impact.

Implementation tasks (high level):
- T1: Template engine schema + storage (templates with variables and priority rules).
- T2: Wire up SLO snapshot API for runtime signals (SLO team contract).
- T3: Integrate with alert-grouping to call template engine when a new grouped incident is created.
- T4: Implement 3 automation primitives (weight adjuster, per-route limit, circuit-breaker tweak) behind feature flags and RBAC.
- T5: End-to-end tests in chaos lab; test harness should simulate region loss and verify automation rollback.
- T6: Observability: SLO dashboard panel, audit log table, and a mitigation-health metric (mitigations.success_rate).
- T7: Docs / on-call training: add abbreviated runbook cheat-sheets to Confluence + 2 training sessions for on-call.

Acceptance test checklist:
- PRs merged for template engine and two automation primitives.
- Staging run shows pages reduced >= 40% for synthetic blips during 48h test window.
- Automated rollback exercised and confirmed in chaos lab.
- Operator UI displays runbook within 30s in 95th percentile of incidents.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged alpha in staging (engineering ops only) for 2 weeks.
2) Internal beta with on-call volunteers in production on low-traffic namespaces for 1 week.
3) Full internal rollout with monitoring thresholds and kill-switch.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Automation causes customer-visible capacity loss. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds (10% shed increments), mandatory canary for cross-region actions, and explicit rollback hotkey.
- Risk: Incorrect template decisions due to stale SLO snapshot. Mitigation: require real-time SLO fetch and include last-fetched timestamp in the template header.

Links / artifacts:
- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RLE/Adaptive+Runbooks
- SLO dashboard (example): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd1234/slo-overview
- Design sketch (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/abcdef/incident-templates
- Implementation PR (starter): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12345

Operational notes:
- Add a mitigation audit stream to the Console (mitigations.audit_stream) and ensure every automated action includes operator, reason, and SLO snapshot.
- Add a "safety fence" that disables automation for customers with enterprise_security flag set.
